motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to approve the Consent Agenda with the exclusion of Items 10.A., 10.B., and 12.A., to be voted on separately, and with Item 13.A. removed and placed under Scheduled Items. The motion also included minor spelling updates to Item 13.B. as discussed during the Policy Session . Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda approved, with items pulled out
motions.summary: The council took up the consent agenda, holding three items back for separate votes, moving item 13.A to open discussion, and correcting spelling in 13.B.
motions.impact: Routine housekeeping — nothing changes for residents. This just sorts which items get a quick group vote and which get discussed on their own.

motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to approve the remaining items on the Consent Agenda , specifically Items 10.A., 10.B., and 12.A . Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.outcome: passed by a vote of 3 :0, with one abstention.
motions.headline: Three consent items approved separately
motions.summary: The council approved consent agenda items 10.A, 10.B and 12.A on their own, apart from the rest of the consent agenda.
motions.impact: This is procedural housekeeping. The motion names the items only by number, so it does not say what they cover or who they affect.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Authorizing Extended Hours for Construction Operations for QTS – SLC1 as Allowed in Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 8.15.080(G).
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Authorizing Extended Hours for Construction Operations for QTS – SLC1 as Allowed in Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 8.15.080(G). Councilmember Huish seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Longer construction hours for the QTS SLC1 site
motions.summary: The council considered allowing the QTS – SLC1 project to run construction outside the hours city code normally allows.
motions.impact: If you live near the QTS SLC1 site, crews could be working earlier or later than the usual limits. The motion does not say which hours or how long they would apply.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain, Utah, Approving the 5 th Amendment to the Amended and Restated Overland Master Development Agreement .
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain, Utah, Approving the 5 th Amendment to the Amended and Restated Overland Master Development Agreement conditioned on the following: 1. Lighting fixtures shall be 25 feet in height instead of 30 feet; and 2. Completion of the SITLA (State School and Institutional Trust Lands Administration) Land Exchange A greement and all agreements related to the bypass road 35 -acre land exchange with SITLA . Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Overland development deal amended; lights capped at 25 feet
motions.summary: The city approved the fifth amendment to the Overland development agreement, requiring 25-foot light poles instead of 30 and a 35-acre land swap with the state.
motions.impact: If you live near the Overland project, streetlights there will be 25 feet tall rather than 30. The agreement only takes effect once the state land exchange for the bypass road is finished, so nothing changes on the ground yet.
